rows.search: Second pass, whole law. Scope: the whole of חוק-יסוד: הממשלה, התשנ״ב-1992 (direct election of the Prime Minister; passed 18.3.1992; in force from the 1996 election; replaced by the 2001 re-enactment from the 16th Knesset), not only its s. 58 amendment of Basic Law: The State Economy, which the first pass covered. Sources in the sheet's order. (1) Hayut survey, HCJ 5658/23, Versa node/705, now read in full (characters 0-353340): the surveyed challenges to Basic Laws are Bergman, Agudat Derekh Eretz, Rubinstein, Mizrahi Bank, Bar-On, Academic Center, Shafir, HCJ 2905/20 (rotation), Scheinfeld, Hasson, Ben Meir; the 1992 Government law and HCJ 5160/99 are not mentioned; the tail mentions Basic Law: The Government (Amendment No. 6), ס״ח תשנ״ז 114, on ministers holding another citizenship, with no petition. Bar-On HCJ 4908/10, Versa, now read in full (0-112680): cites HCJ 5160/99 as a review of Amendment No. 9 to the 1992 law (removal of the cap on ministers) for the proposition that a Basic Law's motives are not, as a rule, a ground for judicial review; Rubinstein J.'s para. 3 recounts the 1999 proposal and his 19.7.1999 letter as Attorney General ('I cannot say that there is a legal bar to this'). (2) Hebrew Wikipedia חוק יסוד: הממשלה (1992) (title without hyphen; the hyphenated title is a 404): passage 18.3.1992 after return from committee, third reading 55-32, entrenchment of 61 MKs in each reading, 1999 removal of the ministers cap, 2001 repeal 72-37; it names no petition or case. IDI articles 9889 (direct-election law) and 7766 (repeal process): no petition. Hamichlol pages on the 1992 law and on the 2001 special election: 403. (3) Petitioners' lists: not browsed; MQG and IDI documents surfaced only through searches. (4) Versa: topic page 'Basic Law: The Government' (first 100000 of 911550 characters) lists only HCJ 7846/19; Versa domain searches on the 1992 law, direct election, 5160/99, Avni, Paritzky and transitional government returned Yesh Atid (HCJ 3132/15), the Olmert petitions (HCJ 7375/06, 9617/06), Weiss, Fuchs, MQG v. Sharon, Litzman, Bar-On, HCJ 5658/23 (citing HCJ 1384/98 Avni and HCJ 932/99), and the citation HCJ 5160/99, IsrSC 53(4) 92 (1999); Versa Weiss page read. Nevo and supremedecisions.court.gov.il: not reachable. (5) Nine Hebrew press and web searches on the law's title and on 'הבחירה הישירה' with בג״ץ, עתירה, בטלות, חוקתיות, 'שימוש לרעה בסמכות המכוננת', 'סעיף 56', the 2001 special election and the candidacy rules: none returned a petition or appeal attacking the 1992 law or any of its provisions as invalid, non-binding or an abuse of constituent power.
rows.related_cases: HCJ 5167/00 Weiss v. Prime Minister (25.1.2001; Barak, S. Levin, Or, Mazza, Zamir, Türkel, Englard; five petitions; denied 6-1): applied ss. 23(c), 31(a)-(b) and 32 of the 1992 law (continuity of a resigned Prime Minister and ministers before the special election of 6.2.2001); no party attacked the law's validity. HCJ 2257/04 Hadash-Ta'al Faction v. Chairman of the Central Elections Committee for the 17th Knesset, PD 58(6) 685 (8.8.2004): interpreted the gap left by Amendment No. 8 (1999); the amendment was not attacked. HCJ 3132/15 Yesh Atid v. Prime Minister (2016): petitioners relied on the deletion, in 2001, of the 1992 provision allowing the Prime Minister to head a ministry; denied by majority. HCJ 1384/98 Avni v. Prime Minister (1998): cited on Versa as a case under the 1992 law; holding not verified. HCJ 5160/99 Movement for Quality Government in Israel v. Constitution, Law and Justice Committee, IsrSC 53(4) 92 (1999): petition against Amendment No. 9 to the 1992 law (a separate enactment in the frame, row 55), not the 1992 law as passed. A Versa snippet also names HCJ 971/99 as reviewing the same kind of amendment; not verified.
rows.note: The 1992 law as passed: direct election of the Prime Minister on a separate ballot together with Knesset elections (first applied 1996), candidacy by nomination of factions of at least ten MKs or 50,000 voters, special elections for Prime Minister alone in defined cases (held 6.2.2001), 8-18 ministers and up to 6 deputy ministers, dissolution of the Knesset on no confidence or budget failure, entrenchment by a majority of MKs in each reading (s. 56), and s. 58 amending Basic Law: The State Economy (s. 3B). Vote on passage: 55-32 per Hebrew Wikipedia; IDI article 9889 gives 57-56 'in 1991', probably an earlier reading. Repealed by the 2001 re-enactment (7.3.2001, 72-37). No petition against the 1992 law itself, its entrenchment, its candidacy rules, its 1996 and 1999 elections or the 2001 special election was found.

deviations: HCJ 5160/99: the judgment text was not reached; the subject (Amendment No. 9, ministers cap), citation IsrSC 53(4) 92 and the propositions it is cited for come from Bar-On (Versa) and Versa search snippets; the formal disposition (dismissal) is inferred and should be verified. HCJ 971/99, named in one Versa snippet as reviewing the same amendment, was not verified.
Versa topic page 'Basic Law: The Government' is 911550 characters; only the first 100000 were read; the remainder may list more cases.
Hamichlol pages returned 403; the Hebrew Wikipedia article exists under 'חוק יסוד: הממשלה (1992)' (no hyphen) and was read.
Petitioner case lists were not browsed systematically; their files surfaced only through web searches, none concerning the 1992 law.

Knesset records are geo-blocked and web.archive.org is unreachable from the fetch tool, so the ס״ח 1396 text of the 1992 law and its amendments were not read; provisions are described from Hebrew Wikipedia, the ICL English text and the Versa Weiss translation.

HCJ 1384/98 Avni v. Prime Minister is recorded only as a case cited under the 1992 law; its holding was not verified. Other 1996-2001 cases that applied the direct-election regime were not individually traced beyond Weiss, Avni and the citations above.
The vote on passage differs between sources (55-32 per Hebrew Wikipedia; 57-56 per IDI article 9889, dated there to 1991); not resolved.
Searches run in this pass: 19 tool calls.
